cards.prompt: how does backpropagation work?
cards.title: Backpropagation Mechanics

diagrams.describe:
Backpropagation carries the loss gradient backward
Read input $x$ → Compute hidden activations $h$
Compute hidden activations $h$ → Compute prediction $\hat y$
Compute prediction $\hat y$ → Evaluate loss $L$
Evaluate loss $L$ — Start backward pass → Differentiate loss at prediction
Differentiate loss at prediction — $\partial L/\partial \hat y$ → Apply chain rule at output layer
Apply chain rule at output layer — $\partial L/\partial h$ → Apply chain rule at hidden layer
Apply chain rule at hidden layer — Gradients for both layers → Update weights $w\gets w-\eta\nabla_w L$
The backward pass reuses saved activations. At each layer, multiply the incoming loss gradient by local derivatives.

spec.caption: The backward pass reuses saved activations. At each layer, multiply the incoming loss gradient by local derivatives.

cards.prompt: how does backpropagation work?

diagrams.describe:
Backpropagation carries the loss gradient backward
Read input $x$ → Compute hidden activations $h$
Compute hidden activations $h$ → Compute prediction $\hat y$
Compute prediction $\hat y$ → Evaluate loss $L$
Evaluate loss $L$ — Start backward pass → Differentiate loss at prediction
Differentiate loss at prediction — $\partial L/\partial \hat y$ → Apply chain rule at output layer
Apply chain rule at output layer — $\partial L/\partial h$ → Apply chain rule at hidden layer
Apply chain rule at hidden layer — Gradients for both layers → Update weights $w\gets w-\eta\nabla_w L$
The backward pass reuses saved activations. At each layer, multiply the incoming loss gradient by local derivatives.

cards.prompt: how does backpropagation work?
sketch: Forward pass makes a prediction -> the loss compares it with the label -> gradients flow backward layer by layer (chain rule).
Each weight moves opposite its gradient (w - eta * gradient); this repeats for every batch.
cards.title: Backpropagation Mechanics

diagrams.describe:
Backpropagation carries the loss gradient backward
Read input $x$ → Compute hidden activations $h$
Compute hidden activations $h$ → Compute prediction $\hat y$
Compute prediction $\hat y$ → Evaluate loss $L$
Evaluate loss $L$ — Start backward pass → Differentiate loss at prediction
Differentiate loss at prediction — $\partial L/\partial \hat y$ → Apply chain rule at output layer
Apply chain rule at output layer — $\partial L/\partial h$ → Apply chain rule at hidden layer
Apply chain rule at hidden layer — Gradients for both layers → Update weights $w\gets w-\eta\nabla_w L$
The backward pass reuses saved activations. At each layer, multiply the incoming loss gradient by local derivatives.

cards.prompt: how does backpropagation work?
sketch: Forward pass makes a prediction -> the loss compares it with the label -> gradients flow backward layer by layer (chain rule).

diagrams.describe:
Backpropagation calculates gradients via chain rule
Read input $x$ → Compute hidden activations $h$
Compute hidden activations $h$ → Compute prediction $\hat y$
Compute prediction $\hat y$ → Evaluate loss $L$
Evaluate loss $L$ — Start backward pass → Differentiate loss at prediction
Differentiate loss at prediction — $\partial L/\partial \hat y$ → Apply chain rule at output layer
Apply chain rule at output layer — $\partial L/\partial h$ → Apply chain rule at hidden layer
Apply chain rule at hidden layer — Gradients for both layers → Update weights $w\gets w-\eta\nabla_w L$
The forward pass computes outputs, then the backward pass computes gradients using local derivatives.
